creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Split out of a_26LAtezW0. herdr holds a pane's terminal at whatever geometry its controlling client asked for, and does not put it back when that client goes: measured 53x23 -> 120x40 -> still 120x40 ten seconds after detach (docs/observations/herdr-0.8.0.md section 4, corpus/herdr-0.8.0/geometry/).

No client can work around it properly, only paper over it. The size a pane had before is not recoverable from the API - herdr publishes rows as scroll.viewport_rows and columns nowhere at all - so the best any client can do is hand the pane back at the rectangle herdr's own layout gives it, which Muster now does on quit. That is a guess at what herdr wants rather than a restoration, and it is one every client would have to make.

Worth raising upstream: it reads as a defect rather than a design, and it sits directly against sessions outliving their clients. Whether to file it, and in whose words, is Alex's call - this card is the proposal, not the issue.
title: 🔼 herdr keeps a pane's PTY at the size a detached client set
